subject: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Mills <diane.mills@acme-analytics.com>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement

Hi Diane / Acme SRE team,

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, we're proposing a controlled patch/upgrade for your private VPC deployment next week. High-level asks and proposals below so we can align on the maintenance window, pinning semantics, and rollback criteria.

Summary (short):
- Target window: Tue 2028-04-03 02:00–04:00 UTC (3 hour buffer incl. pre/post checks)
- Version pinning: customer pin to Redwood runtime v2.11.3 for 30 days post-upgrade, automatic minor security backports allowed
- Canary: 10% traffic canary for 60 minutes with health checks; 50% ramp at 2h, 100% at 4h if green
- Rollback: automated rollback trigger on 3 consecutive 5-min SLO breaches or 2 critical errors in telemetry

Action items for Acme: share on-call rotation for the window, confirm acceptance of the pinning clause and whether you want us to request a temporary SLA exception/credit for the window. I've attached a draft maintenance plan and a rollback playbook.

Technical notes / concerns for our ops team:
- Networking: we plan a short ephemeral route refresh on the control plane for instance switchover; will coordinate with your netops to ensure iptables/NSG rules are stable.
- Data path: no data migrations expected; KV caches will be invalidated for new model kernels.
- Secrets & KMS: no key rotation in this window. If you require HSM rewraps, flag now.

Please review the attached plan. If the window doesn't work, propose an alternate time. Diane — if you want Redwood to run the canary only on non-prod traffic first, we can accommodate (we'll need a mapping).

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-maintenance-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), private-rollback-playbook.md (text)

From: Diane Mills <diane.mills@acme-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre-team@acme-analytics.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the detail. A few quick clarifications before I share with NetOps: 

1) The window looks OK but our preferred blackout for reporting is 03:00–06:00 UTC (we can extend your buffer). Can you shift the start by +1 hour?
2) On pinning: we agree to pin to v2.11.3 for 30 days, but we require that any security backports are reviewed by our security lead (we can do a standing exception to allow patch-only rollups).
3) Rollback conditions: can you define "5-min SLO breach" — is that p95 latency > 300ms or an error rate bump?

I'll confirm NetOps availability by EOD. Also, we'll need the rollback playbook to include exact Playbook runbook steps we can run from our side (API endpoints, required RW tokens).

Best,
Diane
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Mills <diane.mills@acme-analytics.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 19:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement

Diane — thanks, and all good to shift. Answers inline below.

On Fri, Mar 30, 2028 at 17:03 Diane Mills <diane.mills@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> 1) The window looks OK but our preferred blackout for reporting is 03:00–06:00 UTC (we can extend your buffer). Can you shift the start by +1 hour?

Yes — we can shift the window to 03:00–05:00 UTC primary, with our prechecks starting at 02:30 and post-verification until 06:00. I'll update the attached plan.

> 2) On pinning: we agree to pin to v2.11.3 for 30 days, but we require that any security backports are reviewed by our security lead (we can do a standing exception to allow patch-only rollups).

Understood. We'll implement a pin that blocks feature/behavior changes while allowing security-only backports. We will send the patch diff to acme-security@acme-analytics.com prior to applying; acceptance can be a simple ack. We'll add a short review SLA (4 hours) in the plan.

> 3) Rollback conditions: can you define "5-min SLO breach" — is that p95 latency > 300ms or an error rate bump?

Good catch. Proposed concrete triggers:
- Latency: p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows OR p95 > 350ms
- Error rate: 2x baseline 5xx rate sustained over a 10-minute window OR immediate detection of critical errors (>0.1% of requests returning 5xx with customer impact flag)
- Data integrity alarms (any failed commit to persistent store) -> immediate rollback

Rollback mechanics (summary):
- Canary failed: automatic rollback to previous pinned variant for canary pool (automated)
- Full rollback: orchestrated by Redwood ops with a fail-open manual confirmation. We will provide API token instructions in the playbook so Acme can trigger the rollback from their runbook.

I'll attach a one-page SLO/triggers cheat-sheet to the plan and set up an API token scope for rollback-only actions.

--
Karthik

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement

Thanks for drafting. Two operational asks from my side before we give Acme the 'go':

1) Monitoring: add a dedicated canary dashboard (p95, p50, 5xx rate, kernel memory, kv-cache hit rate) that updates at 15s granularity and is viewable by Acme SRE with read-only links.
2) Escalation path: include a single pager with on-call phone/SMS for the 1st/2nd/engineering leads and a 15-minute RTO commitment for rollback initiation.

If those are in the playbook, +1 from me. Also confirm we won't rotate instance IPs for more than 30s during the switchover (NetOps concern).

-Vivek
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Diane Mills <diane.mills@acme-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, sre-team@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 09:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: ops mechanisms and fallback agreement

Appreciate the quick updates — Acme NetOps and Security reviewed the plan. Two final confirmations: 

• We accept the 03:00–05:00 UTC primary window with your extended pre/post checks; our NetOps will be on call for the kick (John Harper).
• We approve the 30-day pin with security-backports only policy, pending the 4-hour review SLA. Acme will provide the security mailbox acme-security@acme-analytics.com for diffs.

Please update the spreadsheet (acme-maintenance-plan.xlsx) with the final API token name and add Vivek's monitoring dashboard link. If you can send an updated doc and a short runbook excerpt (commands and endpoints) by EOB today, we'll sign the maintenance approval and attach it to our change ticket.

—Diane
